[[Arad, Romania|Arad Municipality]] | chairman = Florian Voinea | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Adrian Mihalcea]] | league = [[Liga I]] | season = [[2025–26 Liga I#Play-out round|2025–26]] | position = Liga I, 7th of 16 | website = {{URL|http://www.uta-arad.ro/|uta-arad.ro}} | current = 2026–27 FC UTA Arad season | kit_alt1 = | pattern_la1 = _utaarad2627h | pattern_b1 = _utaarad2627h | pattern_ra1 = _utaarad2627h | pattern_sh1 = _nikeleague3ur | pattern_so1 = | leftarm1 = FFFFFF | body1 = FF0000 | rightarm1 = FFFFFF | shorts1 = FF0000 | socks1 = FF0000 | kit_alt2 = | pattern_la2 = _niketrophy6gw | pattern_b2 = _niketrophy6gw | pattern_ra2 = _niketrophy6gw | pattern_sh2 = | pattern_so2 = | leftarm2 = FFFFFF | body2 = B0B0B0 | rightarm2 = FFFFFF | shorts2 = B0B0B0 | socks2 = B0B0B0 }} '''Asociația Fotbal Club UTA Arad''' ({{IPA|ro|ˈuta aˈrad}}), commonly known as '''UTA Arad''' or simply '''UTA''' (''Uzina Textilă Arad''; {{lit|Textiles Factory of Arad}}), is a Romanian professional [[Association football|football]] [[football team|club]] based in the city of [[Arad, Romania|Arad]], [[Arad County]] that competes in the [[Liga I]], the top tier of [[Romanian football league system|Romanian football]]. The team was founded in 1945 as ''IT Arad'', and has won six national titles and two [[Cupa României]]. Domestically, UTA is one of the most successful Romanian sides of the 20th century,{{cite journal|last=Adam|first=Robert|title=Football and authoritarianism in twentieth century Romania: between propaganda and subversion|journal=Soccer & Society|volume=21|issue=6|year=2020|pages=657–666|doi=10.1080/14660970.2020.1775043|hdl=2013/ULB-DIPOT:oai:dipot.ulb.ac.be:2013/328285|hdl-access=free}} sharing with [[Chinezul Timișoara]] the record for the most title wins by a club not from [[Bucharest]], earning it the nickname ''Campioana Provinciei'' ("Provincial Champion"), a record which ended after the conclusion of the [[2020–21 Liga I|2020–21 season]] when [[CFR Cluj]] claimed its seventh Liga I trophy. UTA Arad's decline began with a transfer to the [[Liga II|second division]] in 1979, after which it rarely appeared in the top flight before being dissolved in 2014. UTA Arad was eventually promoted from the [[Liga IV]]{{cite web|url=http://sportarad.ro/membrii-cu-drept-de-vot-in-scu-inclusiv-bara-au-decis-drepturile-federative-trec-la-uta-batrana-doamna-care-va-deveni-uta-arad/|title=Membrii cu drept de vot în SCU, inclusiv Bara, au decis: drepturile federative trec la UTA Bătrâna Doamnă care va deveni UTA Arad!|language=ro|trans-title=Members with voting rights in SCU, including Bara, decided: federative rights are passed to UTA Bătrâna Doamnă, which will become UTA Arad!|publisher=sportarad.ro|date=16 March 2014|archive-date=17 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160317011010/http://sportarad.ro/membrii-cu-drept-de-vot-in-scu-inclusiv-bara-au-decis-drepturile-federative-trec-la-uta-batrana-doamna-care-va-deveni-uta-arad/|url-status=dead}} and managed to return to the Liga I in 2020. The team plays in red and white [[Kit (association football)|colors]] at the new [[Stadionul Francisc von Neuman|Francisc von Neuman Stadium]], which was opened in 2020. UTA holds a long-standing rivalry with neighbouring [[SSU Politehnica Timișoara]], with whom it contests the [[West derby (Romania)|West derby]].{{refn|group=note|name=Steaua|The original [[FC Politehnica Timișoara]] was dissolved in 2012; after that, SSU Politehnica Timișoara and [[ACS Poli Timișoara]] were created, but the latter was also disbanded in 2021. In any case, SSU inherited the fanbase and holds the original brand.}}"}}
